A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GScenes and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 contains no appendix; v2's Appendices A–G contain both relocated and new material. The complete supplied documents support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-reconstruction, qualitative ablation, and pose-estimation results in Section 4, Figures 5–6, and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments on MipNeRF360 and DL3DV, alongside qualitative and quantitative model ablations in Section 3 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V2 replaces DUSt3R initialization with MASt3R and B-spline view sampling with an elliptical trajectory. It replaces instruction conditioning with camera Plücker embeddings, extends the existing FiLM conditioning to geometry, adds confidence-weighted RGBD encoding, and revises classifier-free guidance to use image and confidence signals. These substantially change the reconstruction and generation procedures.

E1.justification: V2 adds DL3DV-10K training data while dropping DTU and LLFF from the stated fine-tuning mixture. Evaluation expands beyond the retained nine MipNeRF360 scenes to 15 DL3DV benchmark scenes and an explicitly reported CO3D plant qualitative comparison (Section 3.1 and Appendix D).

E2.justification: InstantSplat in v1 Tables 1–2 is replaced by MASt3R + 3DGS, an actual initialization change rather than a rename. The other principal baselines remain. V2 additionally evaluates a cross-attention variant and a diffusion variant using 3DGS-Enhancer's confidence measure (Figure 6 and Table 3).

E3.justification: Reported diffusion fine-tuning increases from 10k to 100k iterations, with 28,161 samples from 165 scenes replaced by 171,461 samples from 1,043 scenes. Guidance changes from image/text scales of 2.5/7.5 to image/confidence scales of 3.0/3.0. V2 introduces a DL3DV view-selection protocol and changes the principal ablation settings from Counter/Treehill with six or nine views to Bonsai/Treehill with three views.

E4.justification: V1's qualitative confidence, instruction, and depth ablations are substantially replaced by context/confidence and FiLM-versus-cross-attention comparisons, including a new six-metric quantitative table. V2 also adds tests of up-block conditioning and alternative confidence conditioning (Figures 5–6). The pose-error analysis is retained, moving from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's newly disclosed shared noise latent across novel views concerns inference consistency, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially revise GScenes and baseline scores and add DL3DV results; v2 also adds quantitative ablation results. For the revised GScenes configuration, three-view MipNeRF360 PSNR/FID become 13.809/163.747, replacing 14.976/253.659. Changed methods and training prevent treating these as controlled performance gains. DiffusioNeRF's three-view PSNR also changes from 13.134 to 9.996 without an explained cause. The pose-error values remain identical.

T1.justification: V2 adds the mathematical definition of its camera-level Plücker/Fourier encoding and revises the conditioning and guidance equations. The confidence formula, autoencoder objective, and scene-reconstruction loss remain substantially unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from instruction-following diffusion without explicit camera conditioning to geometry-conditioned RGBD generation using MASt3R. V2 explicitly emphasizes FiLM efficiency relative to cross-attention and an open-source, low-cost contribution. The overarching pose-free reconstruction goal and competitiveness claims remain.

C2.justification: The pose-error and multiview-consistency limitations remain, but their explanation changes: v1 emphasizes absent view conditioning, whereas v2 discusses autoregressive synthesis despite camera conditioning. Appendix G adds dependence on the rendering distribution and MASt3R versus SfM initialization. Section 3.3 also acknowledges that the geometry-only baseline can outperform GScenes on conventional metrics.

D1.justification: V2 adds camera-embedding dimensions and Fourier-band counts, FiLM/cross-attention parameter counts, initial point-cloud size, and shared-noise implementation information. Reported fine-tuning time changes from one to four GPU days, while v1's explicit diffusion timestep schedule disappears. V2 newly describes GScenes as open source but supplies no project or code-access link.

R1.justification: Appendix B newly identifies Paul et al. (2024) as the closest predecessor and explains extensions involving pose-free reconstruction, RGBD modeling, conditioning, and confidence. It expands pose-free research positioning and adds relevant references such as BARF, DBARF, and Light Field Networks. The introduction and Figure 2 prominently reposition GScenes around accessibility and lower resource requirements relative to closed-source competitors.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and method exposition, reorganizes architecture and conditioning into dedicated subsections, and expands the algorithm description. Background, related work, and limitations move into appendices, while the main narrative is restructured. V1's duplicated diffusion-background explanation is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds a first-page teaser, method-comparison matrix, trajectory visualization, new diagnostic figures, and extensive qualitative comparisons. Pipeline diagrams are redrawn, benchmark tables gain dataset groups and pose-status markers, and a quantitative ablation table is added. Existing material is also resized or relocated, including the reduced VAE comparison and appendix pose-error table.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper through second-benchmark evaluation, quantitative design comparisons, clearer method documentation, and explicit positioning against its closest predecessor. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Table 4 retains v1's pose errors and DUSt3R caption despite the MASt3R switch, and the blanket generative-metric superiority claim overlooks DL3DV nine-view DISTS of 0.189 versus the baseline's better 0.187. The evidence supports a limited net quality improvement.
